BILL NUMBER:  S5538

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the state finance law, in relation to bids for the
purchasing of services or commodities by state agencies submitted by
bidders who do business with a nation identified as a state sponsor of
terrorism


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
Authorizes within the bid process for any New York State Request for
Proposal (RFP), any company - foreign or domestic - that submits a
bid, must disclose if they or any of their subsidiaries - foreign or
domestic - do business with any state sponsors of terrorism. New York
State will reserve the right to reject the lowest and best bid should
the company been found to do business with a country identified as a
state sponsor of terrorism.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
Section 1. State finance law is amended a new section 169.

Subdivision 1 mandates state agencies to require each bid submitted
shall disclose whether or not the bidder, or any subsidiary of such
bidder, has ever engaged in business with a nation identified as a
state sponsor of terrorism. The State agency may reject such bid if
the bidder discloses having done business with a state sponsor of
terrorism.

Subdivision 2 defines the term "nation identified as a state sponsor
of terrorism" as Iran, North Korea, Sudan and Syria.

Subdivision 3 includes companies that the comptroller determines
provide military equipment to any domestic party in such nations
including its government and rebels.

Subdivision 4 excludes companies that the comptroller determines
either directly or through an affiliated instrumentality provide
services clearly dedicated to social development for the whole nation.

Section 2. This act shall take effect immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :
This legislation would authorize within the bid process for any New
York State Request for Proposal (RFP), any company - foreign or
domestic - that submits a bid, must disclose if they or any of their
subsidiaries - foreign or domestic - do business with any state
sponsors of terrorism. New York State will reserve the right to reject
the lowest and best bid should the company been found to do business
with a country identified as a state sponsor of terrorism.

Nations that have been identified as state sponsors of terrorism pose
a threat to our state and our country. Because of this, state agencies
should have the ability to reject a bid from a company that has done
or is currently doing business with one of the nations. This
legislation takes the necessary steps to provide a disincentive to
companies to do business with terrorist nations. Exemptions are
provided for those companies who provide services clearly dedicated to
social development in such nations. Such services include, but are not
limited to, providing medicine and medical equipment, agricultural
supplies and infrastructure, educational opportunities,
journalism-related activities, and general consumer goods.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
New bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.
